stanzas: 好一朵茉莉花，好一朵茉莉花，满园的花开赛不过了它，本待要，采一朵戴，又恐怕看花的骂；本待要，采一朵戴，又恐怕看花的骂。

What a fine jasmine flower, what a fine jasmine flower; of all the flowers blooming in the garden, none can outdo it. I meant to pick one to wear, but I fear the one who tends the flowers would scold; I meant to pick one to wear, but I fear the one who tends the flowers would scold.
Hǎo yī duǒ mòlìhuā, hǎo yī duǒ mòlìhuā, mǎn yuán de huā kāi sài bù guò le tā, běn dài yào, cǎi yī duǒ dài, yòu kǒngpà kān huā de mà; běn dài yào, cǎi yī duǒ dài, yòu kǒngpà kān huā de mà.
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (Hanyu Pinyin (tone marks))

notes: The edition prints the whole song as one line, and so do the English and the romanization. It is in simplified characters.
'好一朵' (hǎo yī duǒ): an exclamation, 'what a fine (single) flower'; 朵 is the measure word for flowers.
'赛不过了它' (sài bù guò le tā): 'cannot outdo it, cannot surpass it'.
'本待要' (běn dài yào): 'I had meant to, I was about to'.
'看花的' (kān huā de): 'the one who watches over the flowers', the garden's keeper; 看 read kān ('guard'). Singers often say kàn ('look at'), which would make it 'those who come to look at the flowers'.
rom: base tones written (一 yī, 不 bù), not the sandhi forms yí/yì and bú that are sung.
